title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in New Orleans, LA: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for New Orleans refinery, shipyard and aerospace welders: ASME, D1.1 or D17.1 for Part C. Corporate, online or one-to-one.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in New Orleans: Six Days for Refinery, Shipyard and Aerospace Welding Inspectors
html:
Greater New Orleans welds an unusual range of things. Rocket stages take shape inside a NASA plant in the east of the city, Navy landing craft leave a shipyard on Chef Menteur Highway, refineries line the Mississippi from Chalmette upriver to Garyville, and a new container terminal is planned downriver in St. Bernard Parish. Each of those jobs needs people who can judge a weld against a written requirement, and the credential most employers recognize for that is the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI).

Atlantis NDT runs a six-day (6-day) exam-preparation course for the CWI, covering Part A Fundamentals, Part B Practical and Part C Code Application. It is offered three ways: corporate delivery at the employer's facility, online study for individuals, and one-to-one sessions with the instructor. AWS administers the CWI examination and issues the certification; the course gets candidates ready and Atlantis certifies no one. There is no Atlantis classroom in New Orleans and no venue to visit, since Atlantis keeps its two offices in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India. Questions about format or fit can go through the New Orleans CWI enquiry form.

How the six days work for a New Orleans candidate

All three formats share one outline. Fundamentals fill the first two days: processes from shielded metal arc to submerged arc, terminology to AWS A3.0, joint design, symbols to AWS A2.4, metallurgy, destructive testing, how discontinuities form, an overview of NDT methods, safety, fabrication math and the duties of an inspector. Day three is practical preparation with gauges and specimens, day four works inside your Part C code book, day five is timed practice papers, and day six closes whatever gaps those papers reveal. A day-by-day view is on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

  • Corporate. A refinery contractor, shipyard, steel fabricator or aerospace supplier preparing several staff has the six days delivered at its own facility, with its welds and gauges and, where it suits, its code and procedures.
  • Online. An individual receives a study plan built on the six-day outline, course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and can send questions to an instructor throughout. Nothing runs at a set hour; you decide the pace.
  • One-to-one. A single candidate takes six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor, either online or in person at a location agreed when booking.

The practice material is Atlantis's own work, written against the topic areas AWS publishes, and not one item is lifted from an AWS examination. AWS has not approved or endorsed the course.

Where the welding happens around New Orleans

Aerospace at NASA's Michoud Assembly Facility

Michoud, in New Orleans East, is one of the largest manufacturing plants in the country. NASA describes an 829-acre site with a main building covering 43 acres under one roof, managed by the Marshall Space Flight Center. Boeing leads construction of the Space Launch System core stage there, and Lockheed Martin builds the Orion crew module pressure vessel, which is welded on site. NASA says Michoud's friction stir welding tool is the largest of its kind, and its Vertical Assembly Center joins domes, rings and barrels into core stage tanks before the finished welds are examined nondestructively.

Hardware like this is welded in aluminum alloys to NASA and customer specifications, with traceability and documentation far beyond ordinary fabrication. AWS D17.1, the specification for fusion welding in aerospace applications, is the Part C option closest to that world. Friction stir welding has a separate AWS aerospace specification, D17.3, which is not one of the Part C choices.

Shipyards from New Orleans East to the Bayou Region

Textron Systems' shipyard on Chef Menteur Highway designs and builds the Ship-to-Shore Connector for the U.S. Navy, and in April 2026 the company announced further investment across its Louisiana sites, including facilities in Slidell supporting armored vehicle work. An hour or two southwest, the Bayou Region has become a center of government shipbuilding. Bollinger Shipyards in Lockport holds the Coast Guard contract for a new class of Arctic Security Cutters, Thoma-Sea also builds in Lockport, Conrad Shipyard works out of Amelia, and Saronic Technologies is expanding in Franklin to build autonomous surface vessels. Industry leaders there have named welders as the bottleneck, and at least one regional initiative aims to train 500 welders over five years.

Navy and Coast Guard ships are welded and inspected to government specifications and classification rules rather than to an AWS code, and the CWI does not replace those requirements. Yard quality departments still value it, because it shows an inspector understands processes, distortion, discontinuities, symbols and accurate measurement before learning the contract documents.

Refineries on the river

Louisiana's refinery survey lists Chalmette Refining in Chalmette, Valero's refinery in Meraux, Valero's plant at Norco, the Norco refinery once operated by Shell and now held by Equilion Enterprises, and Marathon's refinery at Garyville. Together they generate constant maintenance welding and periodic turnarounds, all of it under ASME Section IX for qualifications and B31.3 for process piping. Alloy steels, heat treatment records and hardness limits make the inspector's paperwork as important as the visual check.

The port and the Louisiana International Terminal

Port NOLA's wharves, terminals and rail links keep structural welders busy with repair and extension work. The bigger change is downriver. The Louisiana International Terminal, a container terminal planned near Violet in St. Bernard Parish with partners Terminal Investment Limited and Ports America, received its federal permit from the Army Corps of Engineers in August 2026 and is aiming to open in 2028. Wharf steel, crane rails and terminal buildings mean a long run of structural work under AWS D1.1.

Flood protection, bridges and buildings

Floodgates, pump stations and drainage structures around the city contain welded steel that is repaired and replaced over long programs. The river crossings and the interstate network need bridge steel fabricated under AWS D1.5. Hospitals, hotels and public buildings add structural steel to D1.1, and on larger projects the building code calls for special inspection of structural welding.

Who hires CWIs around New Orleans

  • Refinery maintenance and turnaround contractors along the river, who need ASME-literate inspectors all year and many more for outages.
  • Shipyards and their subcontractors, from New Orleans East to Lockport and Amelia, where QC inspectors check fit-up, welding and visual acceptance before NDT and testing.
  • Aerospace contractors and suppliers connected with Michoud, where welding documentation and traceability are scrutinized closely.
  • Structural steel fabricators such as Southland Steel Fabricators, which donated weld test plates for the AWS New Orleans Section's 2025 student competition.
  • Port, marine and civil contractors building wharves, terminals and flood-protection structures.
  • Inspection and engineering firms providing source and third-party inspection. Atlantis's field work in the city is described on weld inspection services in New Orleans.

Picking the Part C code for New Orleans work

Part C is the open-book code paper, and AWS lets each candidate pick the book. The menu runs from AWS D1.1 (structural steel), D1.2 (aluminum), D1.5 (bridges), D15.1 (railcars) and D17.1 (aerospace) to API 1104 for pipelines, an ASME package of Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. New Orleans spreads its candidates across more of that list than most cities do.

Main line of workCode bookReason
Refinery and chemical plant piping, turnaroundsASME packageMatches the qualification and piping codes used inside the river plants.
Shipyard structure, port and terminal steel, buildingsAWS D1.1The broadest structural code and a common choice for yard and fabrication inspectors, even where government specifications govern the ship.
Aerospace hardware and its suppliersAWS D17.1The aerospace fusion welding specification, closest to Michoud work.
Aluminum fabrication, workboats and structuresAWS D1.2For inspectors whose work is mainly structural aluminum.
Pipelines across the deltaAPI 1104Federal pipeline safety rules incorporate it for welding and acceptance.

Study the edition AWS lists on your application; it is often a step behind the latest printing. More background: AWS D1.1, ASME Section IX, API 1104, AWS D1.5 and the guide to procedure and welder qualification. Atlantis does not write or qualify welding procedures, but a CWI has to check work against them.

The AWS New Orleans Section

New Orleans has an active AWS section in District 9. Its 19th annual student welder competition, held in November 2025 at New Orleans Pipe Trades in Metairie, drew students from Delgado Community College, Nunez Community College, Independence High Magnet School and Southeastern Louisiana University, with Lincoln Electric donating prizes and consumables. The same month, the section's general meeting took place at Delgado's River City campus in Avondale, where the welding program director spoke about curriculum and job placement and an Ironworkers Local 623 journeyworker described her route from welding student to ironworker.

For a CWI candidate, evenings like these are where you meet QC managers and senior inspectors who can tell you how local employers view the credential, which code they expect, and who might confirm your welding history for the AWS application.

Where New Orleans welders train

Delgado Community College offers Certificates of Technical Studies in flux cored and gas metal arc welding, shielded metal arc welding, and gas tungsten arc welding, each roughly nine months long, with NCCER Level 1 and 2 credentials and AWS SENSE built in and an advisory committee of regional employers shaping the skills taught. Nunez Community College in Chalmette runs a welding program as well, including one for justice-involved youth delivered with the Louisiana Office of Juvenile Justice. The pipe trades and ironworkers apprenticeships train many of the welders who end up on refinery and structural jobs.

Those programs feed straight into CWI eligibility. AWS treats completed trade or vocational courses as education that shortens the experience requirement, and an apprenticeship or college record is the easiest evidence of welding-related work to put in front of AWS. None of these schools is an Atlantis partner or venue; they are part of how the city builds welders, and many local CWIs started there.

Booking the exam from New Orleans

The sequence starts with your AWS application. When AWS accepts it, you receive a confirmation letter with an eligibility code, which Prometric needs before it will book your computer-based papers: Part A, 150 questions on fundamentals, and Part C, roughly 50 to 65 open-book questions on your chosen code. AWS reports more than 100 Prometric centers across the US, and you book whichever one suits your schedule. The practical, Part B, does not happen at Prometric. AWS delivers it itself, with hands-on tasks using equipment it provides plus 46 questions, at its own seminar and examination locations, and if no session falls near Louisiana when you are ready, you travel to one. Every part needs 72% or better.

AWS lists its examination and seminar fees on aws.org. To plan the total, including books, travel and unpaid days, use the CWI exam cost planner, and read the part-by-part results article to see which part catches people out.

Studying around turnarounds, shipyard schedules and hurricane season

River plant turnarounds, shipyard production schedules and the June-to-November hurricane season compete for the same months. A shipyard inspector on a fixed shift has predictable evenings; a turnaround hand may lose a month at a time; a storm can pull everyone into repair work. The online plan copes with all three because it has no timetable. Fundamentals can be spread over a few weeks of evenings, code-book drills fit into breaks if you keep the book at work, and Part B measurement practice needs little more than a set of gauges and some scrap welds. Keep the timed papers for the run-up to your Prometric booking, and send questions to the instructor whenever they arise. If you would rather have someone setting the pace, one-to-one sessions can be booked around the days you have free.

Corporate: six days at a New Orleans-area employer

For a group, the six days come to the employer. A refinery contractor might run the course in its yard office for pipefitters and QC staff heading for the ASME book; a shipyard might prepare a QC team on D1.1 using its own panel and stiffener welds; an aerospace supplier might split the code day between D17.1 and D1.2. The practical day uses the company's own gauges and real production welds, so measurement practice matches daily acceptance work. Timing can avoid outages, launches and delivery milestones. Each candidate still deals directly with AWS for eligibility, the vision record, the application and the bookings.

One-to-one sessions, online or in person

One-to-one suits a candidate whose situation does not fit a plan: an engineer who needs the CWI for a quality role at a contractor, a foreman who has not sat an exam in decades, or someone retaking a single part. Six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor can run online or in person at a location agreed when you book, and the time goes where you need it most, usually the weakest fundamentals topics and the chosen code book.

Eligibility and the vision record

Two requirements sit outside any course. The first is documented experience: AWS sets the years of welding-related work by education, five with a high school diploma, one with a bachelor's degree in welding engineering or welding technology, and more with less schooling. The full table is on the CWI exam prep page. The second is the AWS Visual Acuity Record, covering near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more (corrective lenses allowed) and color perception, examined by a qualified practitioner within the period AWS allows before your exam. Contract work makes the first harder than it sounds, so start a list of employers, sites, dates, processes, codes and a supervisor contact for each job now. Short of the years? The CAWI lets you work under a CWI's supervision while you build them; the CWI requirements guide explains how.

After the CWI: New Orleans career paths

A CWI stays valid for nine years under AWS rules, with renewal filings at the third and sixth years. What comes next depends on where you work. Shipyard inspectors often move toward QA supervision; aerospace inspectors deepen their specification and traceability skills; refinery inspectors sometimes pursue API in-service inspection credentials, which API administers and Atlantis does not train for. Experienced inspectors can aim for the AWS Senior CWI; the SCWI pathway explains the step.

Adding nondestructive testing is another common route, especially ultrasonic testing for shipyard and aerospace work. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you through its written practice once training and method experience are complete, and Atlantis provides that training: see NDT training in New Orleans, UT Level 2, MT Level 2 and VT Level 2. The CWI, API 577 and ASNT Level II comparison shows how the credentials differ, and Practical NDT offers simulated inspection practice. For local inspection work, see ultrasonic testing in New Orleans and maritime NDT consulting in New Orleans.

Other Gulf Coast CWI pages, and your quote

Candidates across the region can also read the CWI exam prep pages for Baton Rouge, Lake Charles, Mobile and Houston.

To get a quote, say how many people want to prepare, whether each prefers corporate, online or one-to-one, which code book each is aiming for, and a short outline of their schooling and welding background. For delivery at your facility, include the address, the gauges and sample welds available, and any outage or launch dates to avoid. Atlantis prices each request individually and gives a quote on request; use the New Orleans CWI quote request.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in New Orleans?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in New Orleans; Atlantis has offices in Houston and Hyderabad. You can study online with an instructor answering your questions, have the six days delivered at your employer's facility, or book one-to-one sessions online or in person. The course page has the outline.
AWS administers the examination, decides eligibility and issues the certification. Atlantis prepares candidates, has no view of the exam questions, and its course is not approved or endorsed by AWS.

faq.q: Which Part C code suits a refinery inspector on the river?
faq.a: Usually the ASME package, which covers Section IX welding qualification alongside the B31.1 and B31.3 piping codes used in the Chalmette, Meraux, Norco and Garyville plants.

faq.q: I inspect at a shipyard. Which code book should I take?
faq.a: Most yard and fabrication inspectors take AWS D1.1, and aluminum specialists may prefer D1.2. Navy and Coast Guard ships still follow their own government specifications, which the CWI does not replace.

faq.q: Is there a Part C option for aerospace work like Michoud?
faq.a: Yes. AWS D17.1, the aerospace fusion welding specification, is one of the Part C choices. AWS D17.3, which covers friction stir welding, is not a Part C option.

faq.q: Where do New Orleans candidates sit the exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based tests booked at a Prometric center with the eligibility code in your AWS confirmation letter. Part B, the practical, is run by AWS at its own seminar and examination locations, so you may need to travel.

faq.q: Can a shipyard or refinery contractor have the six days delivered at its facility?
faq.a: Yes. Corporate delivery brings the six days to your site, uses your gauges and production welds, and can split the code day between books. Each candidate still applies to AWS personally. Ask for a quote.

faq.q: How does one-to-one work, online or in person?
faq.a: You get six days of sessions with the instructor on your own. They can be held online or in person at a location agreed when booking, and the time is weighted toward your weak areas and your code book.

faq.q: Do the practice questions come from AWS?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes them from the AWS topic lists, and none is taken from a real examination.

faq.q: Does a Delgado welding certificate count toward eligibility?
faq.a: Completed trade or vocational training can lower the experience AWS requires, typically from five years to four, but AWS decides which education row applies. Delgado is not connected with the Atlantis course.
